XP 600
N Medium animal
Init +0;
Senses low-light vision; Perception +5

DEFENSE

AC 16, touch 10, flat-footed 16 (+6 natural)
hp 22 (3d8+9)
Fort +6, Ref +3, Will +2 (+4 vs. disease and poison)

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft.

Melee bite +6 (1d8+4+1d4 acid plus disease) or claw +5 (1d4+3)
Space 5 ft.; Reach 5 ft.

STATISTICS

Str 16, Dex 10, Con 16, Int 1, Wis 12, Cha 2
Base Attack +2; CMB +5; CMD 15
Feats Run, Weapon Focus (bite)
Skills Acrobatics +4, Perception +5, Survival +5

Disease

Red Ache Bite-injury; save Fortitude DC 15; onset 1d3 days; frequency 1/day; effect 1d6 Str damage; cure 2 consecutive saves

ECOLOGY

Environment deserts or plains
Organization solitary or feasting group (2-5)
Treasure none

This very odd, bipedal reptile is mostly a mouth.

Maws are an odd creature that consists of a reptilian, tailless body on two strong legs. The head comprises most of the torso and is largely the gaping mouth. They are omnivorous and will eat nearly anything they come across. Their voracious appetites and aggressiveness make them a general nuisance to nearby societies.

Author’s note on the maw: While I realize that the inspiring creature does not deal acid damage with it’s bite, I was pondering how an animal could work if most of it’s body is its mouth. I came up with that they digest their food in their mouth rapidly. This would require a much higher acid content in their saliva, hence, acid. If you want to stick closer to the source material, remove the acid damage and increase the bite damage to 1d10 (or 2d8 for the horned maw).
